detail.title: Service Delivery Manager- Digital Workplace Solutions
detail.location: Morrisville, North Carolina, United States of America
detail.jobDescription:
The Service Delivery Manager (SDM) is a customer-facing role within the North America Digital Workplace Solutions (DWS) Service Management Office (SMO), reporting to the Senior Manager, Service Management Office. The SDM is responsible for the successful delivery, governance, and operational management of one or more strategic customer accounts, ensuring service commitments are consistently achieved while fostering strong customer relationships.

Acting as the primary interface between the customer, delivery teams, account leadership, and executive stakeholders, the SDM drives operational excellence, service quality, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement across the customer lifecycle. The role is accountable for service performance, governance execution, risk management, financial stewardship, and ensuring alignment between customer expectations and delivery outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Customer Relationship Management

  • Serve as the primary service management contact for assigned customer accounts.
  • Develop and maintain trusted relationships with customer stakeholders, including operational leaders, executives, and key business contacts.
  • Lead regular customer governance meetings, service reviews, operational reviews, and executive business reviews.
  • Ensure customer concerns, risks, and escalations are addressed proactively and resolved in a timely manner.
  • Advocate for customer needs while balancing contractual commitments, operational requirements, and business objectives.
  • Support customer satisfaction, retention, and growth initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance service performance and customer outcomes.

Service Delivery & Governance

  • Own service management governance for assigned accounts, ensuring adherence to established SMO operating standards.
  • Monitor and manage service performance against contractual commitments, SLAs, KPIs, and operational objectives.
  • Facilitate regular operational reviews with delivery teams to assess performance, identify trends, and address areas requiring improvement.
  • Drive accountability across cross-functional delivery teams to ensure service commitments are achieved.
  • Ensure accurate and consistent service reporting, including performance metrics, risk assessments, action plans, and customer communications.
  • Maintain visibility into program health, dependencies, issues, and operational risks.

Incident, Risk & Escalation Management

  • Serve as the service delivery lead for customer escalations and major service issues.
  • Coordinate cross-functional response teams to address high-priority incidents and service disruptions.
  • Drive root cause analysis activities and ensure corrective and preventative actions are implemented.
  • Identify and mitigate delivery, operational, and customer experience risks before they impact service performance.
  • Provide clear and timely communication to customer and internal stakeholders during critical situations.

Continuous Improvement & Service Excellence

  • Identify opportunities to improve service quality, operational efficiency, and customer experience.
  • Lead service improvement initiatives aligned to customer priorities and operational objectives.
  • Support the implementation of standardized processes, governance models, and best practices across the DWS organization.
  • Leverage data and analytics to identify trends and recommend actionable improvements.
  • Drive adoption of automation, AI-enabled capabilities, and process simplification opportunities where appropriate.

Financial & Contractual Management

  • Partner with account leadership and finance teams to support revenue, margin, and cost management objectives.
  • Monitor contract performance and ensure services are delivered within agreed scope and commercial parameters.
  • Identify and manage scope changes, risks, assumptions, and service dependencies that may impact financial performance.
  • Support forecasting, budgeting, chargeback validation, and change order activities.
  • Provide visibility into financial risks and opportunities affecting assigned accounts.

Program & Project Coordination

  • Collaborate with project managers, transition teams, and operational leaders to support customer initiatives and transformation programs.
  • Ensure operational readiness for new services, projects, and program changes.
  • Coordinate across delivery towers to ensure successful execution of customer priorities.
  • Support organizational transformation initiatives and service modernization efforts.

Executive & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with Sales, Delivery, Operations, Engineering, PMO, Finance, Procurement, and Customer Success teams.
  • Provide account health updates, risk summaries, and operational insights to leadership.
  • Contribute to account planning, customer strategy discussions, and business reviews.
  • Support account growth and renewal activities through strong operational performance and customer advocacy.

detail.title: Head of AI Architecture
detail.location: Morrisville, North Carolina, United States of America
detail.jobDescription:
About Our Team

Lenovo’s Intelligent Devices Group (IDG) AI Ecosystem Team is seeking a Head of AI Architecture & Innovation to define and deliver the architecture of Lenovo’s next-generation AI ecosystem. 


We recently introduced Qira, our new cross‑device Personal AI that works seamlessly across Lenovo and Motorola products.  More information can be found here: https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/lenovo-unveils-lenovo-and-motorola-qira/


What You'll Do

• Own the architecture across the full software development and delivery cycle of AI experiences, spanning cross-device runtimes, hybrid AI execution, orchestration and knowledge frameworks, model runtimes and tuning, platform services, observability, security and Infosec compliance, release and OTA rollouts, partner enablement, and incubation.

• Ensure Lenovo’s AI features are designed for delivery at scale: performant, secure, reliable, observable, and privacy-conscious across millions of devices.

• Guide integration of hybrid model execution across local devices and cloud, with routing, fallback, and policy enforcement.

• Define standards for release engineering, pipelines, governance, and rollback mechanisms.

• Drive cross-team architectural alignment, making pragmatic tradeoffs to keep features shippable.

• Partner with inter-department Infrastructure and Infosec teams to remove bottlenecks and ensure compliance.

• Mentor senior engineers and ICs, raising technical depth and execution focus across the org.

• Ensure the architecture is future-proof and extensible, enabling SDKs, 3P agent integrations, and experimental innovation.


Basic Qualifications

• 15+ years of software engineering and architecture experience delivering large-scale, production-grade systems

• Experience with the full AI stack: experience surfaces, agentic orchestration, knowledge and memory systems, perception, model runtimes, evaluation, and infrastructure.

• Proven track record of shipping AI-driven or distributed software systems at scale.

• Experience architecting cross-device runtimes (Windows + Android) with cloud integration.

• Proven expertise in delivering software with OTA rollouts and preload governance at global scale.

• Expertise in designing complex distributed systems and cloud-native platforms, with broad knowledge across cloud providers (infrastructure, APIs, observability, and deployment).


Preferred Qualifications

• Deep expertise in the Microsoft ecosystem and Azure cloud including architecture, services, and enterprise-scale integration.

• Strong understanding of hybrid AI architectures, including local and cloud inference, model orchestration, and multimodal runtimes.

• Experience guiding globally distributed engineering organizations in agile or scaled agile (SAFe) environments.

• Recognized as a pragmatic software architect who enables engineering teams to deliver, not just design.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any federal, state, or local protected class.

The successful candidate will lead and manage complex, multi‑tower services engagements across Lenovo’s full Solutions & Services Group (SSG) portfolio, including Infrastructure Managed and professional services - including Hybrid Cloud, DaaS, IaaS, Digital Workplace Solution and Security. The SSE will orchestrate customer‑centric solutions that address business outcomes while effectively bringing forward the breadth and depth of Lenovo’s services capabilities.

This is a client-facing sales role; industry sales experience, the ability to identify, consultative engagement, close net new business, and expertise are required. We are looking for an acquisition seller with a proven track record to take their career and our solutions and services business to the next level. The candidate will also evaluate customer opportunities as presented in RFPs/RFQs or engagements from the Services and Hardware Sales teams and use this information to manage the sales engagement process to ensure we meet the customers’ requirements. Lenovo solutions can include Services, Hardware, Software, Security, ISVs, and additional 3rd Party Services from Lenovo Business partners.

This role will provide dedicated support across our Eastern US acquisition efforts. While the position is fully remote, we are seeking candidates located within or near the region to ensure strong alignment with regional hiring needs, time zones, and stakeholder collaboration. Candidates should be comfortable working remotely while partnering closely with cross-functional teams across the Eastern U.S. territory.

Responsibilities:

Sales Expertise:

  • Opportunity identification - develop, implement, and execute an effective sales strategy to achieve sales goals
  • Partner across multiple organizations including, but not limited to, sales; finance; service delivery; customers and business partners and lead all elements of the services sales cycle
  • Define framework to manage long term strategy & forecasting by effectively and consistently use Microsoft Dynamics and other reporting tools to track key sales metrics and consistently meet those metrics
  • Manage complex contract negotiations and Account Engagement (Strategic Responsibilities)

This includes aligning Lenovo’s full services portfolio to the customer’s business priorities and ensuring a coordinated approach to achieving territory and segment goals.
  • Cultivate and expand executive‑level relationships, jointly with the Client Manager, positioning Lenovo as a trusted strategic advisor. Leverage business insights and services expertise to influence customer vision, guide strategic initiatives, and reinforce Lenovo’s value across the enterprise.

Portfolio Acumen:

  • Display deep understanding of E2E strategic portfolio of services across the entire portfolio
  • Ability to understand customers’ business and IT challenges and position the appropriate Lenovo solutions
  • Ability to position complex solutions - across Lenovo's extensive services portfolio

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in relevant field or equivalent professional work experience
  • 8+ years of success selling IT services and solutions, with a focus on:
    • Large, multi-year managed services contracts
    • Complex, consultative sales cycles

Preferred Requirements:

·       Strong knowledge of Digital Workplace Solutions and Device as a Service.

  • Experience as an IT Services Solutions provider selling multi-year managed services solutions
  • Exceptional communication, presentation, and negotiation skills.
  • Self-motivated, results-oriented, and able to work independently.

detail.title: Channel AI Technical Business Development Manager
detail.location: Morrisville, North Carolina, United States of America
detail.jobDescription:
Candidates may be based anywhere, with preference for those located near a major airport to facilitate travel requirements.


The Partner AI Technical Business Development Manager serves as the primary technical liaison and strategic catalyst between the organization and key channel partners. Focused on driving adoption of NVIDIA AI platforms and AI Factory architectures, this role bridges complex high-performance infrastructure with channel growth. 

You will educate partner teams, serve as the technical authority for AI factory sizing and solution design, and articulate the financial and strategic value of Lenovo partnership programs to executives, sales teams, and architects.


Scope of Work

  • Technical Engagement: Direct technical consultation for channel partners designing and deploying NVIDIA-powered AI Factory architectures.
  • Enablement & Training: Ownership of delivering technical and sales training curricula covering Lenovo's AI portfolio and NVIDIA accelerated computing stack.
  • Go-To-Market (GTM) Co-Selling: Alignment with partner sales teams to identify, qualify, and win large-scale AI infrastructure deals.
  • Strategic Partner Advocacy: Drive alignment across Lenovo partner programs, incentive structures, and co-selling motions to maximize partner profitability and engagement.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

Technical Architecture & Solution Design

  • Serve as the primary technical backstop for sizing, architecting, and configuring AI Factories, including compute (NVIDIA HGX platforms), networking (InfiniBand/Spectrum-X Ethernet), storage, and power/cooling requirements.
  • Assist partner Solution Architects in validating custom AI workloads, AI Factory sizing and design, and reference architectures.
  • Translate customer AI requirements into scalable, Lenovo-integrated hardware and software stacks.

Partner Enablement & Evangelism

  • Evangelize the value of Lenovo AI platforms and NVIDIA software suites (such as NVIDIA AI Enterprise, NeMo, and Omniverse) across partner sales and engineering organizations.
  • Conduct technical bootcamps, workshops, and certifications for partner solution architects and presales engineers.

The Lenovo Global Future Leaders Program is a highly selective program designed to develop Lenovo's next generation of business and technology leaders. As a Global Future Leader, you'll gain hands-on experience through challenging assignments and rotational opportunities across Lenovo. During your first three years, you'll participate in cross-functional experiences, strategic projects, leadership development, and mentorship opportunities designed to accelerate your growth.   • Exposure to senior leaders along with structured leadership development and mentorship
  • Collaboration with global teams and stakeholders across one of the world's leading technology companies
  • Accelerated career growth through innovation, continuous learning, and opportunities to influence the future of smarter technology for all

In This Global Future Leader Role, you will act as an AI Solution Architect


Role Overview

Lenovo is seeking a motivated early-career professional to join our AI Library team as an AI Solution Architect. This role is ideal for a recent or upcoming graduate who is passionate about Artificial Intelligence, technical solution design, and using technology to solve real-world customer challenges.  


As an AI Solution Architect, you will help translate business needs and customer requirements into scalable, reliable, and repeatable AI solutions built on Lenovo’s AI Library. Working alongside senior solution architects, engineers, business analysts, sales teams, and partners, you will gain hands-on experience across the full AI solution lifecycle—from discovery and design to validation, readiness, and customer deployment. This role offers a unique opportunity to grow as a technical architect while helping shape Lenovo’s growing AI solution portfolio.


What You’ll Do

  • Assist in designing end-to-end AI solutions that leverage Lenovo infrastructure, platforms, and services.  
  • Help create reference architectures, solution blueprints, and patterns for common AI use cases.  
  • Support senior architects in defining components, data flows, integration points, and security considerations.  
  • Align technical designs with customer requirements, performance needs, and Lenovo standards.

AI Library Solution Development & Readiness

  • Contribute to the development and refinement of AI Library offerings to ensure they are modular, reusable, and scalable.  
  • Assist in evaluating partner AI solutions for inclusion in the AI Library from an architectural perspective.  
  • Help translate innovative AI concepts into standardized solution packages that can be delivered globally.  
  • Support creation of implementation guides, deployment runbooks, and technical documentation.

Technical Validation & Delivery Support  

  • Participate in proof-of-concept (PoC) activities and solution validation with engineering teams.  
  • Assist in testing, performance tuning, and optimization of AI solution components.  
  • Support readiness activities to ensure solutions can be deployed consistently by delivery and services teams.  

Pre-Sales & Cross-Functional Collaboration  

  • Work with sales and senior architects to understand customer challenges and map them to AI solutions.  
  • Help prepare technical presentations, architecture diagrams, and solution overviews for internal and external stakeholders.  
  • Gather feedback from customers, field teams, and partners to inform improvements to AI Library offerings.  

What You’ll Learn

  • How enterprise AI solutions are designed, validated, and brought into production at scale.  

  • The interactions between AI models, data pipelines, infrastructure, platforms, and security in real-world architectures.  

  • Best practices for building reusable reference architectures and repeatable AI solution patterns.  

  • How solution architects work with sales, product, marketing, and services to drive customer adoption.  

  • Practical approaches to translating business requirements into technical designs and trade-offs.  

  • Customer-facing and executive communication skills from a solution architecture perspective.  



Job Requirements  

  • Recent or upcoming Bachelor’s graduate; Master’s degree preferred in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or related technical fields.  
  • Passion for AI, emerging technologies, and applying solution architecture to real-world business challenges.  
  • Foundational understanding of AI and data concepts (e.g., machine learning, generative AI, data pipelines) gained through coursework, projects, or internships.  
  • Exposure to programming and/or data technologies (e.g., Python, SQL, APIs, cloud platforms) preferred.  
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to structure and decompose complex problems.  
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with comfort working across technical and non-technical teams.  
  • Familiarity with AI tools (e.g., Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT) and analytical tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) is a plus.

GLF Program Requirements

  • Currently completing or recently completed a degree from an accredited university (Bachelors, Masters or PhD)
  • Passion for technology, innovation, and continuous learning
  • Demonstrated leadership potential through academic, professional, internship, or community involvement
  • Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving capabilities
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence and work effectively across global teams

About Our Team

We are seeking an AI Product Manager to help define, build, and deliver the next generation of Lenovo AI experiences. In this role, you will own key product experiences from discovery through launch, working closely with engineering, design, research, product planning, business development, and other product leaders. You will combine a deep understanding of users with an understanding of rapidly evolving AI technologies to identify opportunities, define product requirements, make thoughtful product tradeoffs, and turn emerging AI capabilities into intuitive, differentiated experiences for millions of users.

This is an opportunity to join a growing AI organization and play a hands-on role in shaping how AI comes to life across Lenovo's ecosystem of devices and services.


Location: Chicago, IL (Hybrid; 3 days onsite, 2 days remote)


What You'll Do

• Own the strategy, roadmap, requirements, and execution for key AI-powered product experiences across Lenovo devices and services.

• Identify meaningful user problems and determine where AI can create differentiated, high-value experiences.

• Translate product strategy and user needs into clear product requirements, priorities, user stories, and success metrics.

• Partner closely with engineering, design, research, and other cross-functional teams throughout the product development lifecycle, from concept and prototyping through launch and iteration.

• Work directly with AI technologies, including generative AI, large language models, AI agents, multimodal experiences, and cloud- and device-based AI capabilities.

• Evaluate emerging AI technologies and models and determine how they can be applied to real-world consumer experiences.

• Use market research, competitive analysis, user research, product analytics, and customer feedback to inform product decisions and identify new opportunities.

• Balance user experience, technical feasibility, business impact, privacy, security, performance, and cost when making product decisions.

• Define and track product KPIs and use data and experimentation to continuously improve experiences after launch.

• Collaborate with product planning, strategy, business development, and partner teams to develop product strategy and business cases for new opportunities.

• Work across Lenovo's device portfolio to create experiences that take advantage of the broader Lenovo ecosystem.

• Communicate product vision, priorities, tradeoffs, progress, and results clearly to stakeholders and senior leadership.

• Stay current on the rapidly evolving AI landscape and bring new ideas and technologies into Lenovo's product roadmap.


Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, Design, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 12+ years of product management experience delivering software, digital, or technology products.

• Demonstrated experience owning products or major product features from concept through launch and ongoing iteration.

• Experience working closely with engineering, design, and other cross-functional teams to deliver user-facing products.

• Experience translating customer needs and complex technical capabilities into clear product requirements and compelling user experiences.


Preferred Qualifications

• Experience building AI-powered products or experiences, particularly products involving generative AI, large language models, AI agents, multimodal AI, personalization, or conversational interfaces.

• Experience with consumer technology, consumer electronics, mobile, web, Android, Windows, or cloud-based products.

• Strong understanding of AI product development, including model capabilities and limitations, evaluation, latency, cost, privacy, safety, and responsible AI considerations.

• Experience working with software, hardware, design, and development teams and navigating the technical constraints of experiences that span devices and cloud services.

• Experience developing products within agile, pod-based, or similarly cross-functional product organizations.

• Experience using rapid prototyping, experimentation, A/B testing, user research, and analytics to validate product hypotheses.

• Strong product judgment and passion for creating simple, intuitive experiences from complex technologies.

• Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment where technology, customer expectations, and product requirements are evolving quickly.

• Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing opportunities and make effective product tradeoffs using data, customer insights, and business objectives.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to influence technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Entrepreneurial mindset with a willingness to move between strategy and hands-on execution.

• Experience working with globally distributed product and engineering teams is a plus.


What Success Looks Like

You will help Lenovo turn rapidly evolving AI capabilities into products that solve meaningful user problems. Successful candidates will be equally comfortable defining a product vision, debating an AI experience with designers and engineers, analyzing user feedback and metrics, and driving the details required to ship a high-quality product.

You will be a product owner who can bring clarity to ambiguity, move quickly from idea to validation, and ultimately deliver AI experiences that users value and want to use every day.


The base salary range budgeted for this position is $180,000 - $190,000. Individuals may also be considered for bonus and/or commission. ​​

detail.title: Sr. Product Manager, System Management Firmware
detail.location: Morrisville, North Carolina, United States of America
detail.jobDescription:
The System Management Firmware Product Manager owns the customer-facing management capabilities delivered through XCC and UEFI, together with the product definition and governance of system-wide firmware packages across the server portfolio. The role sets capability scope and priorities, determines base and premium functionality, and makes enhancement, deferral and retirement decisions in partnership with architecture and engineering on feasibility and implementation.


Scope includes remote monitoring and control, inventory and health, diagnostics, configuration, power and thermal management, security and access control, management APIs, and integration with the wider XClarity ecosystem. It also covers coordinated firmware discovery, update, rollback and lifecycle management across XCC, UEFI and supported devices. Own product decisions on the inclusion and timing of third-party device firmware updates within Lenovo system firmware packages. Apply quality or security requirements established by the accountable teams, and evaluate other updates based on customer value, portfolio benefit, compatibility and lifecycle risk.


The role complements server product managers by owning the horizontal firmware capability roadmap and governance across the portfolio, while individual server product managers retain accountability for the definition, launch and business performance of their server products. The Product Manager translates customer, market, platform and engineering needs into a coherent roadmap, aligns stakeholders, and drives predictable execution across new and sustaining firmware releases and server platforms. Applying server-platform management expertise, the role improves firmware quality, customer experience and business value across the general-purpose server portfolio.


Responsibilities:

  1. Own the Product Strategy and Definition for System Management Firmware

    • Define and own the product vision, roadmap, requirements, feature scope, priorities, positioning, and customer value for Lenovo XClarity Controller (XCC), UEFI, and system management firmware capabilities.
    • Make and document product decisions regarding feature inclusion, prioritization, enhancement, deferral, and retirement while balancing customer needs, business objectives, technical feasibility, lifecycle impacts, and risk.
    • Partner with architecture and engineering teams to ensure firmware capabilities align with platform strategy and customer requirements.

  2. Lead Firmware Lifecycle Management and Portfolio Governance

    • Own the end-to-end lifecycle of firmware management capabilities, including roadmap planning, release management, launch readiness, sustaining engineering, and retirement.
    • Define release scope, readiness criteria, and coordinated execution across quality, security, documentation, manufacturing, support, sales enablement, and field organizations.
    • Govern system-wide firmware packages, including firmware discovery, updates, rollback, compatibility, and lifecycle management across XCC, UEFI, and supported hardware devices.

  3. Drive Cross-Functional Execution and Organizational Alignment

    • Lead coordination across product management, architecture, firmware development, hardware engineering, validation, manufacturing, supply chain, security, support, sales, and marketing teams.
    • Manage dependencies, risks, escalations, and competing priorities to ensure predictable execution and successful delivery of firmware releases.
    • Establish decision-making frameworks and accountability models that clearly distinguish product ownership from technical implementation responsibilities.

  4. Enhance Product Competitiveness and Customer Value

    • Ensure firmware capabilities meet competitive expectations for manageability, security, resiliency, serviceability, performance, power efficiency, and overall customer experience.
    • Monitor customer feedback, adoption metrics, field quality data, and market trends to identify opportunities for innovation, simplification, and differentiation.
    • Own decisions regarding third-party device firmware inclusion and update timing within Lenovo system firmware packages, considering customer value, quality, security, compatibility, and lifecycle impacts.

  5. Leverage Data, Analytics, and Market Insights

    • Establish, maintain, and evaluate key performance indicators (KPIs) related to firmware adoption, update success rates, customer experience, support outcomes, release readiness, and roadmap execution.
    • Maintain high-quality product documentation, requirements, decision records, risk assessments, and supporting materials to ensure traceability and operational excellence.
    • Engage with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders to translate market insights into measurable firmware capability improvements and business outcomes.

  6. Serve as a Subject Matter Expert and Industry Advocate

    • Act as a recognized authority on server management firmware, platform management technologies, and industry trends.
    • Stay current on emerging technologies, standards, and partner roadmaps across CPU, BMC, NIC, storage, RAID, GPU, PCIe, CXL, memory, and related platform technologies.
    • Share expertise, mentor stakeholders, and drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality, operational efficiency, and customer satisfaction.


Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience in server, infrastructure, firmware, platform, software, hardware, or related product management and technical leadership roles
  • Proven track record of defining, delivering, launching, or managing complex technology products, platform capabilities, firmware solutions, or infrastructure offerings throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Strong understanding of server platform architecture and firmware technologies, including BIOS, UEFI, BMC, XCC, platform management firmware, and device firmware.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives across engineering, architecture, validation, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, security, support, sales, marketing, and supplier organizations within a global business environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate risks, manage ambiguity, balance competing priorities, influence stakeholders, and drive product decisions to successful outcomes.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Working knowledge of industry-standard platform management technologies and protocols such as Redfish, IPMI, or comparable management interfaces.
  • Familiarity with platform security concepts, including trust, identity, attestation, cryptographic lifecycle management, firmware security, and secure-update practices.
  • Experience using analytics, KPIs, AI-assisted tools, automation, or data-driven decision-making techniques to improve product planning, execution, and lifecycle outcomes.
  • Knowledge of data center, enterprise, cloud, AI infrastructure, or high-performance computing environments and associated customer requirements.
  • Expertise in emerging server technologies and ecosystem trends, including CPU, BMC, NIC, storage, RAID, GPU, PCIe, CXL, memory, and related platform technologies, with the ability to translate technical developments into product strategy and customer value.

detail.jobDescription:
REPORTS TO
Global Privacy Leader

ROLE FOCUS
Strategic AI ecosystem

FUNCTION
Legal / Global Privacy and Data Protection

TRAVEL
Approximately 10%

Lenovo is seeking an experienced Senior Counsel, Privacy & AI to join its Legal Department and Global Privacy & Data Protection Team. This role will serve as a strategic legal advisor on privacy, artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technology initiatives across Lenovo's worldwide business operations.

This is an embedded, product-facing role providing strategic and day-to-day legal support for AI-enabled products and services, including generative and multimodal AI, AI assistants and agentic capabilities, personalization features, on-device and cloud processing, and third-party integrations. The role will work closely with cross-functional teams and other legal subject matter experts to identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, support product launches, and help drive scalable governance processes.

The successful candidate will combine deep privacy and technology expertise with strong business judgment and technical fluency. Working closely with product, engineering, security, AI governance, commercial legal, regional privacy attorneys, and other legal stakeholders, this attorney will translate complex legal requirements into practical, scalable solutions that enable innovation while appropriately managing legal and regulatory risk.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as a privacy legal advisor for product, engineering, and business teams developing AI-enabled products and services.
  • Provide practical, risk-based guidance throughout the product lifecycle and partner with product, engineering, security, AI governance, and business stakeholders to identify legal and regulatory risks, develop appropriate mitigation measures, and support launch readiness and ongoing governance of AI-enabled products and services.
  • Conduct and support privacy impact assessments, AI risk assessments, and other legal reviews, identifying requirements, mitigation measures, residual risks, and matters requiring escalation.
  • Review and advise on product requirements, architectures, data flows, privacy notices, consent mechanisms, launch plans, and supporting documentation.
  • Draft, review, and negotiate agreements involving AI technologies, data licensing, cloud services, software development, suppliers, and strategic technology partners.
  • Develop and maintain scalable governance frameworks, policies, standards, assessment templates, and review processes supporting privacy and AI compliance programs.
  • Support investigations and response activities involving privacy, data governance, AI, or cybersecurity-related issues.
  • Monitor global legal, regulatory, enforcement, and policy developments affecting AI and emerging technologies and advise stakeholders on business and product impacts.
  • Improve review processes, reduce bottlenecks, and create scalable guidance for recurring issues while maintaining strong documentation and defensible decision-making.

Basic Qualifications

  • Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school.
  • Active license to practice law and good standing in at least one United States jurisdiction.
  • 12+ years of relevant legal experience, including substantial experience in privacy, data protection, product counseling, AI, machine learning, or other data-intensive technologies.
  • Demonstrated experience advising technology, software, digital-service, or AI product teams throughout the product-development lifecycle.
  • Strong working knowledge of U.S. and international privacy and data protection requirements, including GDPR, U.S. state privacy laws, and their application to emerging AI technologies and complex global data flows.
  • Strong technical fluency and ability to understand system architecture, data flows, model documentation, software and cloud integrations, security assessments, and AI-enabled products and services.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, sound legal judgment, and the ability to translate complex legal and technical concepts into practical business guidance.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage multiple complex projects, prioritize effectively, identify and escalate material risks, and thrive in a fast-paced global organization.
  • Privacy and AI governance certifications (CIPP/US, CIPP/E, AIGP, or comparable credentials).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience advising on generative AI, foundation or large language models, multimodal models, AI assistants, agentic systems, retrieval-augmented generation, model training and fine-tuning, model evaluation, or on-device and cloud inference.
  • Experience supporting integrated hardware, software, cloud, and AI ecosystems (such as PCs, smartphones, tablets, connected devices, operating-system integrations, software preloads, applications, APIs, SDKs, and third-party services).
  • Familiarity with AI governance programs and frameworks, including the EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO 27701, or similar standards.
  • Experience advising on biometrics, sensitive personal information, automated decision-making, consumer protection, or AI safety issues.
  • Experience with privacy engineering, data governance, privacy-enhancing technologies, and impact assessment programs.
  • Experience reviewing or advising on commercial agreements involving AI technologies, cloud services, software, data licensing, or technology partnerships.

The Global Account Representative (GAR) is responsible for driving Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) revenue growth, profitability, and customer satisfaction within Lenovo's most strategic Global Accounts. Working in close collaboration with the Global Account Manager (GAM), the GAR serves as the primary ISG sales leader for assigned accounts, developing and executing account strategies that accelerate customer business outcomes and expand Lenovo's footprint across the data center, AI, storage, networking, services, and solutions portfolio.

This is a hunter role with a primary emphasis on creating, developing, and winning net-new business opportunities. The GAR is expected to proactively identify white space opportunities, displace competitors, expand Lenovo's share of wallet, and drive new infrastructure, AI, and services engagements across assigned accounts.

The GAR partners with the GAM, regional sales teams, technical specialists, services professionals, and executive leadership to build trusted customer relationships, uncover and qualify growth opportunities, and deliver winning solutions that address complex business and technical challenges. Success in this role requires strong consultative selling skills, executive engagement, business acumen, forecasting discipline, and the ability to lead through influence in a highly matrixed global environment while maintaining an aggressive focus on business development and market share expansion.

The Lenovo Global Future Leaders Program is a highly selective program designed to develop Lenovo's next generation of business and technology leaders. As a Global Future Leader, you'll gain hands-on experience through challenging assignments and rotational opportunities across Lenovo. During your first three years, you'll participate in cross-functional experiences, strategic projects, leadership development, and mentorship opportunities designed to accelerate your growth. From day one, you'll take on meaningful work, gain exposure to senior leaders, and help drive innovative solutions that deliver smarter technology for all. We're looking for ambitious problem-solvers, innovative thinkers, and future leaders who are energized by technology, embrace new challenges, and are eager to make an impact.

In This Global Future Leader Role, you will act as an AI Platform Engineer (PC Agentic Applications)

 

Role Overview
In this role, you will help build the next generation of Agentic AI applications on PC infrastructure, working alongside senior architects, product leaders, and AI researchers. You will design, prototype, experiment, and scale AI platform capabilities optimized for PC and hybrid deployment environments.

What You’ll Do

detail.title: Technology Incubation – Early Stage Product Manager
detail.location: Morrisville, North Carolina, United States of America
detail.jobDescription:
***Please Note: This is a remote role; however, international travel is expected to collaborate with global R&D labs, business units, and pilot customers, and may reach ~50% depending on project needs and incubation phase. Bay Area is preferred, but remote candidates will be considered.***


About Lenovo CTO Org

Lenovo CTO Org is the cutting-edge R&D and technology incubation organization of Lenovo, dedicated to advancing information technology, smart devices, and services. Our mission is to turn breakthrough innovations into real businesses, powering Lenovo’s most advanced products and services and shaping the future of AI, hybrid computing, edge technologies, and beyond.


About the Role

This role sits at the core of Lenovo CTO Org’s Tech Incubation team, driving end-to-end incubation for early-stage product concepts. You will take opportunities that have initial validation and turn them into real products: shaping MVPs, orchestrating pilots with customers and business units, and managing the path from 0 to 1. Our incubation portfolio spans AI-driven products across robotics, smart manufacturing, full-stack AI agent solutions, sports technology, and other emerging domains. You will own the execution of incubation projects; translating problem statements into product requirements, coordinating R&D and engineering teams, defining success metrics, and driving pilots to clear outcomes that enable scale up.

We seek strategic product thinkers who are also strong operators. People who can combine technology foresight with commercial instincts and then turn that into concrete roadmaps, pilots, and launches. You will work alongside world-class researchers, engineers, and business leaders, bridging the gap between cutting-edge technology development, customer needs, and scalable business outcome.


Key Responsibilities

Market & Commercial Validation:

  • Assess market opportunities for emerging technologies and early product ideas, identifying high potential applications, customer segments, and pain points.
  • Analyze trends, market size, and growth potential to prioritize where incubation effort will have the highest impact.
  • Map the value chain and competitive landscape, including existing and emerging players, investment trends, and potential disruptors.
  • Evaluate business models, pricing approaches, and unit economics to test commercial viability early.
  • Build clear, concise business cases that link customer value, differentiation, and financial outcomes to support investment and scale-up decisions.

Technology Differentiation & Competitive Analysis:

  • Evaluate technology differentiation for incubation projects, articulating why Lenovo’s approach can win versus alternatives.
  • Identify opportunities for platform leverage, technology partnerships, and ecosystem collaboration (e.g., ISVs, cloud, hardware partners) that accelerate time-to-market.
  • Analyze competing and adjacent solutions, providing insights into where we should compete, partner, or integrate.
  • Synthesize findings into clear recommendations and narratives for Lenovo Research leadership and corporate executives, influencing R&D investment, partnership, and product strategy.

Incubation & Pilot Execution:

  • Translate validated opportunities and problem statements into clear product requirements and MVP definitions.
  • Design and drive pilot programs with internal and external customers, from scoping and success-metric definition to execution and post-mortem.
  • Build and manage cross-functional execution plans across R&D, engineering, business units, and partners to hit pilot milestones on time.
  • Collect qualitative and quantitative feedback from pilots, synthesize insights, and turn them into product decisions (iterate, pivot, or stop)
  • Define the path from MVP to scale (productization options, handoff models, resourcing needs) and document clear go/no-go recommendations

What We Look For

  • Strategic mindset with a strong background in technology strategy, early-stage product management, or corporate incubations.
  • Hands-on experience taking products from concept to MVP/pilot, including customer discovery, requirement definition, and basic go-to-market planning.
  • Strong analytical and financial skills, with the ability to assess market viability, competitive positioning, and investment attractiveness.
  • Ability to translate complex technical concepts into simple, actionable narratives and product decisions for executive stakeholders.
  • Experience working in fast-paced, innovation-driven environments where ambiguity is high and learning velocity matters.
  • Passion for emerging technologies, including AI, ML, computing, and digital transformation, and curiosity about how to turn them into real businesses.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in product management, incubation, venture-building, or technology strategy within innovation-driven industries.
  • Proven experience taking products from concept to MVP and pilot, including customer discovery, requirement definition, execution planning, and early go-to-market hypothesis development.
  • Ability to operate in highly ambiguous, early-stage environments, structuring complex problems into clear roadmaps, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
  • Strong commercial and analytical capabilities, including market sizing, competitive landscape evaluation, business model assessment, and unit economics analysis.
  • Demonstrated experience building business cases and translating technical concepts into actionable product decisions and executive-level narratives.
  • Experience collaborating cross-functionally with R&D, engineering, finance, business units, and executive stakeholders.

Summary

This new position joins Lenovo's AI Governance Programs organization within the Chief AI Office (CAIO) in our mission of enabling security and trust in Lenovo's use of AI technology in operations and product development through Responsible AI. The AI Governance Programs organization works across all Lenovo's business and product areas to ensure AI projects and tools are developed and implemented in accordance with Company standards and international regulations.

The candidate should be an experienced governance and program management professional with a strong background in operationalizing security and regulatory requirements across complex technology environments. This role will manage the CAIO AI risk management methodologies, governance processes and assurance capabilities that integrate AI risk management throughout the AI lifecycle. They will collaborate with AI Security, Supply Chain, Legal, Privacy and Ethics so that risks are understood, appropriately managed and transparently reported to CAIO leadership and executive stakeholders.

The candidate should understand the governance and security considerations associated with AI systems and software supply chains, including large language models, agentic AI, third-party AI and security solutions, and emerging regulatory expectations. The ideal candidate can translate AI and security policy, certification, and customer assurance requirements into practical and repeatable operating models, and help demonstrate that Lenovo’s AI systems and products are secure, trustworthy, well-governed, and aligned with internal standards, industry frameworks, and evolving global regulations.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Operationalize AI governance policies, standards and control frameworks across AI platforms and AI-enabled applications.
  • Drive strategic initiatives for Responsible AI, including analysis and risk management of AI projects, agentic AI, LLMs and open weights models
  • Partner with AI Security, AI Privacy, AI Legal, Product Security and Engineering teams to ensure AI and security activities are aligned with regulatory and certification requirements.
  • Monitor compliance with AI governance requirements and support continuous control monitoring, evidence collection and audit readiness.
  • Evaluate emerging AI governance frameworks, industry standards, and regulatory requirements, recommending improvements to Lenovo's AI governance program.
  • Develop governance metrics, dashboards, and reporting to measure AI governance maturity, compliance, and operational effectiveness.
  • Occasional domestic and international travel (approximately 5–20%) for meetings and collaboration.

Basic Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Risk Management, Audit, Law, Data Privacy, Public Administration, Business, Computer Science, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience).
  • 8+ years of experience in cybersecurity, technology governance, risk management, compliance, audit, third-party risk, security assurance, or related fields.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience leading governance, risk, compliance, security assurance, certification readiness, or technology risk reviews involving complex enterprise technology initiatives.
  • Experience working with cross-functional stakeholders including Engineering, Product Management, Security, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, Supply Chain, Third-Party Risk, Enterprise Risk Management
  • Preferred experience conducting security or AI use case reviews, risk assessments, control assessments, or customer assurance reviews.
  • Deep understanding of Responsible AI frameworks and global AI regulations, including the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 27001, NIST AI RMF, OECD AI Principles, or similar governance and assurance frameworks.
  • Good understanding of data protection regulations, including GDPR and privacy-by-design principles, as they apply to AI systems and AI-enabled services.
  • Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, CDPSE, CTPRP, AAISM, ISO 27001 or ISO/IEC 42001 Lead Implementer/Auditor, AIGP, or similar are preferred.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical, regulatory, audit, and assurance topics into clear guidance for technical teams, business leaders, customers, and executives.

We are seeking an experienced AI & HPC Product Line Manager to lead the worldwide product line go-to-market execution for our AI and High Performance Computing (HPC) server portfolio for enterprise and small/medium business (ESMB). This is a high-impact, globally scoped role responsible for translating rapidly evolving AI/HPC technologies and customer requirements into compelling server solutions and differentiated market offerings.

The successful candidate will combine deep technical expertise in AI and HPC hardware and software stacks with strong product management, go-to-market, and commercial skills. The role requires a detailed understanding of NVIDIA accelerated computing technologies, including GPU platforms, networking, software ecosystems, and the broader AI infrastructure stack, as well as the ability to translate technical capabilities into customer value and business outcomes. The candidate must also have breadth into AMD, Intel, ARM, and new AI training and inference offerings in the coming years.

Working across offering group, supply chaing, marketing, sales, channel, alliances, and customers, the Product Line Manager will serve as a key subject-matter expert and business leader for the company's AI/HPC portfolio worldwide, excluding China.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the worldwide product-line strategy for AI and HPC server platforms, from portfolio definition through launch, lifecycle management, and end-of-life.
  • Develop and execute go-to-market strategies that drive revenue growth, market share, customer adoption, and competitive differentiation.
  • Define product requirements and roadmap priorities based on customer needs, industry trends, competitive analysis, technology evolution, and business objectives.
  • Maintain deep technical knowledge of AI/HPC infrastructure, including:
    • GPU-accelerated computing architectures
    • NVIDIA GPU platforms and accelerated computing technologies
    • NVIDIA networking and high-speed interconnect technologies
    • CPU, GPU, memory, storage, and networking architectures
    • AI training, inference, and HPC workloads
    • Cluster architectures and scale-out systems
    • High-performance storage and data pipelines
    • AI/HPC software stacks, frameworks, libraries, and management platforms
    • Cooling, power, density, and data-center infrastructure considerations
  • Develop strong working knowledge of the NVIDIA AI and HPC ecosystem, including relevant hardware, software, platforms, reference architectures, and partner technologies.
  • Partner closely with NVIDIA and other strategic technology partners (Intel, AMD, Broadcom) to understand roadmaps, influence product direction, develop joint solutions, and execute joint go-to-market initiatives.
  • Act as a technical and commercial subject-matter expert for the AI/HPC portfolio, providing guidance to regional sales organizations, solution architects, systems engineers, channel partners, and customers.
  • Work directly with strategic customers to understand their AI/HPC infrastructure requirements and translate those requirements into product and solution opportunities.
  • Enable technical sales teams with compelling product positioning, competitive differentiation, sales tools, presentations, technical content, and customer-facing messaging.
  • Support strategic customer engagements, executive briefings, proof-of-concept activities, benchmark discussions, and major sales opportunities.
  • Develop competitive intelligence and clearly articulate differentiation against other server OEMs, cloud providers, and specialized AI infrastructure companies.
  • Collaborate with engineering and architecture teams to ensure products meet performance, scalability, reliability, manageability, and time-to-market requirements.
  • Partner with marketing to develop product messaging, launches, campaigns, events, white papers, solution briefs, and other market-facing content.
  • Establish and monitor product-line business metrics, including revenue, pipeline, bookings, market share, pricing, profitability, attach rates, and forecast accuracy.
  • Drive cross-functional alignment across worldwide sales, product management, engineering, operations, finance, marketing, and executive leadership.
  • Represent the company at major industry events, customer forums, partner meetings, and technical conferences.
  • Stay current on emerging developments in AI infrastructure, generative AI, accelerated computing, HPC, networking, liquid cooling, disaggregated infrastructure, and data-center architectures.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in product management, product marketing, solutions architecture, technical sales, business development, or a related role within the server, AI infrastructure, HPC, semiconductor, or data-center industry.
  • Demonstrated experience bringing complex technology products to market and developing successful go-to-market strategies.
  • Strong technical understanding of modern AI and HPC server architectures and software ecosystems.
  • Significant hands-on or professional experience with NVIDIA accelerated computing platforms and technologies is required.
  • Strong understanding of GPU computing, AI training and inference, HPC workloads, and large-scale clustered infrastructure.
  • Working knowledge of the broader AI/HPC stack, from silicon and systems through networking, storage, software, orchestration, and workload frameworks.
  • Proven experience working directly with technical sales organizations, solution architects, systems engineers, and enterprise customers.
  • Ability to engage credibly with highly technical customers, engineers, architects, and executives.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.
  • Strong business judgment with the ability to balance technical requirements, customer needs, competitive dynamics, revenue objectives, and product profitability.
  • Willingness and ability to travel internationally as required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with large-scale AI/HPC clusters and data-center deployments.
  • Experience with NVIDIA DGX, HGX, MGX, or comparable accelerated computing architectures.
  • Knowledge of NVIDIA networking technologies and high-speed fabric architectures.
  • Familiarity with CUDA and the NVIDIA software ecosystem, as well as AI frameworks such as PyTorch and related AI/HPC software stacks.
  • Experience with AI infrastructure management, orchestration, benchmarking, and cluster deployment.
  • Experience working with hyperscalers, cloud service providers, research institutions, national laboratories, or large enterprise AI/HPC customers.
  • Experience developing reference architectures or validated solutions with technology partners.
  • Experience managing a global product portfolio across multiple geographic regions.
  • MBA or advanced technical degree is a plus.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable whiteboarding an AI/HPC architecture with an engineer, discussing a GPU platform roadmap with NVIDIA, developing a competitive strategy with product leadership, and presenting the business value of an AI infrastructure solution to a Fortune 500 customer executive.

The IDG AI Ecosystem team is a cross-functional business and technology organization within Lenovo’s Intelligent Devices Group (IDG) responsible for developing, integrating, and commercializing Lenovo’s AI experiences, platforms, agents, applications, and ecosystem partnerships across devices and services. It brings together teams spanning AI architecture, product strategy, user research, software and platform development, ecosystem innovation, and AI-powered experiences such as Qira and other personal and enterprise AI initiatives, with a focus on delivering Lenovo’s “Smarter AI for All” strategy through connected AI solutions that work across devices, edge, cloud, and services. The team also works with AI monetization programs, user research and strategy functions, and participation in broader AI architecture and ecosystem initiatives across IDG.

Position responsibilities include solutions counseling, contract creation, negotiation, and review, providing advice and counsel on legal, compliance and business transactions, including risk analysis and reward.

The position will collaborate with in house and outside counsel, technology experts, marketing and sales teams, product developers as well as with Lenovo’s suppliers and customers as needed.  The successful candidate will have at least 5 years of legal experience in drafting, reviewing, and negotiating a variety of agreements, particularly within a technology company. Strong communication and presentation skills will be necessary to explain complex matters to business partners in a manner that is readily understandable to ensure well-informed business decisions.

  • Partnering with Legal and business leadership to provide risk-balanced, practical legal solutions in the rapidly evolving global AI product ecosystem
  • Strategic advice regarding legal risks in the increasingly fragmented geopolitical technology environment

  • Work closely with clients and the legal team on strategic initiatives in support of all business units

Role Summary

The Senior Manager, AI Control Tower & Agentic AI Governance will serve as the central operating and governance lead for Lenovo’s AI Control Tower and enterprise-scale agentic AI initiatives. This role ensures that new AI agents are business-justified, well-governed, properly supported by data and knowledge assets, and operationally scalable.

The individual will coordinate across DTIT, business units, segments, and functional teams to manage agentic AI intake, governance, prioritization, lifecycle oversight, knowledge base strategy, change management, and value realization. The role is critical to helping Lenovo scale agentic AI safely and efficiently while preventing fragmentation, duplication, and unmanaged AI sprawl.

Key Responsibilities

AI Control Tower & Agentic AI Governance

  • Operate and evolve the AI Control Tower as the central coordination point for enterprise agentic AI initiatives.

  • Establish and manage governance frameworks for AI agent intake, prioritization, risk assessment, lifecycle management, and change control.

  • Coordinate with DTIT to ensure AI agents align with enterprise architecture, security, compliance, and operating model standards.

  • Track and manage the enterprise portfolio of AI agents, including status, dependencies, reuse opportunities, and value realization.

Business Engagement & Enablement

  • Engage business units, segments, and functions to support AI agent design, development, piloting, testing, and adoption.

  • Define training and enablement needs for AI agent deployment.

  • Ensure clear business ownership, success metrics, adoption readiness, and ongoing stakeholder alignment.

  • Act as the primary interface between business stakeholders and DTIT for agentic AI initiatives.

Business Case & Value Validation

  • Partner with business sponsors to validate business cases for new AI agents, including value hypotheses, KPIs, and scale assumptions.

  • Ensure proposed AI agents address clearly defined, high-value use cases.

  • Assess duplication risk and identify reuse opportunities across the enterprise AI portfolio.

  • Track realized value and feed insights back into Control Tower prioritization.

Data & Knowledge Base Strategy

  • Lead engagement with business teams on data sourcing strategy for new AI agents.

  • Own intake and governance for new product or domain-specific knowledge bases, as well as changes, enhancements, and retirement of existing knowledge bases.

  • Coordinate with DTIT on knowledge base setup, seeding, chunking, curation, validation, maintenance, updates, and version control.

  • Serve as the business-facing owner for knowledge asset quality, relevance, and fitness for AI use.

Legacy Data Rationalization

  • Lead structured efforts to inventory and rationalize legacy unstructured data stores.

  • Consolidate content into domain-specific product knowledge bases.

  • Eliminate duplication, stale content, and unmanaged repositories.

  • Drive standards for content ownership, stewardship, and ongoing governance.

Key Interfaces

  • DTIT teams, including architecture, AI platforms, security, data, and change management

  • Business unit and segment leadership

  • Product, sales, services, and operations teams

  • AI platform, knowledge management, and governance functions

Required Qualifications

  • Business degree with MIS or Computer Science background

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise transformation, digital platforms, data/AI governance, and product operations

  • Direct experience working across business units and central IT organizations

  • Strong background in governance, operating models, and portfolio management

  • Demonstrated ability to translate business needs into structured AI, data, and knowledge requirements

  • Proven track record of managing AI projects through the AI solution lifecycle

  • Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Computer Science, MIS, Business Analytics, or AI/ML certification

  • 3+ years of experience with agentic AI, AI platforms, or AI-enabled workflows

  • Knowledge of knowledge bases, unstructured data management, and content lifecycle governance

  • Familiarity with change management frameworks in large, global organizations

  • Experience rationalizing fragmented data or content ecosystems

Critical Success Factors

  • Ability to balance speed and control in AI deployment

  • Strong systems thinking across technology, data, knowledge, and operating model dimensions

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity while creating structure

  • Enterprise-first mindset with business credibility

The base salary budgeted range for this position is $150k - 190K. Individuals may also be considered for bonus and/or commission.

In compliance with Colorado's EPEWA, the expected application deadline for this position is September 27, 2026. This applies to both external and internal candidates.

In partnership with AI and security leaders across Lenovo, the Advisory Engineer, AI Security will lead the technical security architecture and assurance approach for AI models, AI-enabled products and AI development platforms. The role defines secure-by-design patterns, conducts complex security and model assurance reviews, develops technical standards and remediation guidance, and enables consistent adoption across global product and internal-use AI initiatives.

This person is a strategic thinker and strong collaborator who combines leadership and delivery capability with deep technical expertise in AI security. They must be delivery-focused: able to translate AI security strategy, risk findings and technical standards into prioritized work, implementable control requirements, measurable outcomes and sustained adoption across engineering teams.

Hands-on experience designing security architectures and integrating AI systems with enterprise security tools across cloud environments, APIs and data pipelines is essential.

A passion for AI, technology and engineering excellence is critical, with a strong belief that security is built through people, process and scalable technology.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Drive delivery of the AI Security Architecture and Assurance roadmap, defining priorities, milestones, technical deliverables and success measures; track agreed remediation actions through to closure.
  • Define and maintain secure-by-design technical standards, reference architectures, control patterns and assessment methodologies for AI models, LLM and agentic AI systems and AI development platforms.
  • Lead security architecture reviews, threat modelling and technical assurance for high-risk AI systems, products and material changes.
  • Establish and improve model-assurance requirements for third-party and open-weight models, including provenance, supply-chain risk, deployment configuration, vulnerabilities, updates and compensating controls.
  • Define security requirements and technical evaluation criteria for AI security tooling; partner with operational teams on implementation, integration and lifecycle management.
  • Support material AI security incidents and convert lessons learned into improved controls, standards and engineering guidance.
  • Occasional domestic and international travel (approx. 5%) for meetings and collaboration. 

Basic Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, software engineering, mathematics, or a related field
  • 8+ years in product security, application security, cloud security, security engineering or a closely related discipline.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated track record of delivering complex security initiatives from assessment and design through implementation, validation and operational handover, with measurable adoption and risk-reduction outcomes.
  • Experience leading security architecture reviews, threat modelling and remediation through the software or product development lifecycle.
  • Strong understanding of AI security threats and mitigations.
  • Experience designing or assessing security controls across cloud environments, APIs, CI/CD pipelines, identity/access management and data flows.
  • Ability to convert security findings and standards into prioritized technical requirements, clear delivery plans and implementable remediation guidance for engineering teams.
  • Ability to participate in incident response and product security operations as required.
  • Relevant security certifications are advantageous.

This is a hands-on, customer-facing individual-contributor role for a technologist with a business mindset: someone technical enough to configure, integrate, and demo the product, and commercially fluent enough to engage CIOs and CISOs and translate what enterprises actually need back into engineering.

detail.jobDescription:
Job Description

This position is designed for a self-motivated professional with strong knowledge of IT general controls and the capability to test automated controls. The individual will primarily support integrated audits as a senior contributor, independently lead assigned technology audit workstreams, and translate system and control matters into clear business risks and practical insights. The individual may also support general audits based on audit-plan and business needs.

Key Responsibilities:

Project Delivery & Technical Capabilities

  • Apply risk-based thinking to identify, prioritize, and clearly articulate significant technology and business risks.
  • Independently plan and execute assigned audit workstreams, applying sound judgment to risk assessment, scope, testing, analysis, and communication of results.
  • Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of IT general controls and automated controls relevant to the audit objectives and scope.
  • Use data analytics, automation, and approved AI-enabled tools to improve audit coverage, efficiency, documentation quality, and insight generation while complying with Lenovo requirements for security, confidentiality, responsible AI, and professional judgment
  • Prepare accurate, complete, and review-ready workpapers that support clear, evidence-based conclusions. Complete assigned work within agreed milestones and promptly escalate significant quality, scope, evidence, or timeline concerns.
  • Contribute to ongoing scope assessment and raise significant changes in risk or circumstances for timely consideration by the project manager.
  • Support integrated audits by applying IT general controls and automated control testing expertise in the context of the relevant business processes and audit objectives.

Communication & Collaboration

  • Communicate technical risks clearly, concisely, and in business-relevant language to audit leaders, process owners, and technology stakeholders.
  • Lead walkthroughs, testing discussions, and result-alignment meetings for assigned workstreams. Present relevant facts objectively and escalate concerns in a timely manner.
  • Build trusted working relationships across functions, geographies, and cultures while maintaining independence, professional skepticism, confidentiality, and respect.
  • Collaborate effectively with general audit, technical audit, data enablement, subject-matter experts, external audit, and co-source specialists to deliver integrated assurance.
  • Contribute ideas, reusable approaches, and lessons learned that improve audit quality, innovation, and scale.

Business Acumen

  • Develop a practical understanding of Lenovo's strategy, Hybrid AI priorities, operating model, products, services, enterprise systems, and major transformation initiatives relevant to assigned audits.
  • Connect technology risks and controls to business outcomes such as resilience, security, regulatory compliance, data integrity, customer trust, operational efficiency, financial reporting, and strategic execution.
  • Consider enterprise risk, company strategy, stakeholder perspectives, prior audit results, data insights, and external developments when assessing significance and tailoring audit work.
  • Recommend pragmatic and sustainable improvements that address underlying risks and reflect cost, complexity, and business value.

Contribution / Leadership

  • Take ownership of assigned workstreams from planning through reporting and follow-up, with limited supervision.
  • Demonstrate readiness to lead defined phases or smaller engagements when assigned, including coordinating work, tracking milestones, and maintaining quality.
  • Coach less experienced auditors on IT general controls, automated control testing, documentation, and use of audit tools.
  • Actively pursue continuous learning in enterprise systems, technology controls, automated control testing, Lenovo's business, and internal audit practices. Apply learning to improve current work and share it with others.
  • Model Lenovo values, applicable professional standards, ethical behavior, objectivity, and accountability.

Basic Qualifications:

  • University degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Information Systems, Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related discipline.
  • 3+ years of relevant experience in internal audit, external audit, IT audit, IT controls, automated control testing, or a related field. Big Four experience is preferred.
  • Must be able to come into the office x3 a week (Morrisville, North Carolina)
